# Target Architecture: YallaFlow Console > This is a recommendation for owner approval. Nothing here is implemented. > Facts are cited to `CURRENT_STATE_AUDIT.md` and measurements to `PERFORMANCE_AND_SECURITY.md`. > **Revision 2** incorporates an independent architecture review (summarized in §11). The main change from revision 1: the Console now reaches Core through the **CLI's versioned `--json` contract**, not by importing Core modules in-process. ## 1. Decision in one paragraph **[Recommendation]** **Make the CLI the API.** 1. **Core gains:** - versioned **`--json` output** on its read commands, plus one batched `yallaflow snapshot --json`; - targeted **read-path performance fixes**; - later, a **workspace lock**. All three are additive and useful without any Console. 2. **The Console ships as a separate, optional npm package** (`@yallaflow/console`): - a zero-dependency Node `http` server bound to loopback; - it spawns the **user's own installed `yallaflow`** asynchronously, caches the JSON it returns, and refreshes only what a file-watcher event invalidates; - it pushes invalidation events to a **prebuilt** React + TypeScript UI over a header-authenticated event stream. 3. **Writes go through those same CLI commands** (Cycle 3), so the Console cannot diverge from Core's validation, version or locking. 4. **Agents are unaffected.** 5. **Agent control** (chat, monitoring) remains a separate, later, optional adapter package. ## 2. Requirements and how they are met | Requirement | How | |---|---| | The existing CLI stays fully functional | Text output stays the default; `--json` is opt-in | | Existing data stays compatible; no migration | Cycles 1–2 change no existing file's schema. The new artifacts are listed in §6. | | No duplicate source of truth | The Console caches CLI JSON in memory and never persists it as truth | | The UI never edits YAML/JSON directly | The Console has no write path except spawning `yallaflow ` | | Existing validation stays authoritative | It is literally the same process the agent runs | | Read-only actions do not mutate | Measured: no read command writes `.yallaflow/`. `resume`/`handoff` can rewrite `.git/index` through `git status` (fix P6: `--no-optional-locks`). A contract test hashes `.yallaflow/` **and `.git/index`**. | | Local-first; no cloud or model calls | Loopback only, no network, no model calls for reads | | Agent independence | Nothing changes for agents | | Features stay optional | The Console is a separate package; Core keeps its 4 dependencies | | Same YallaFlow version as the agent | The Console resolves `yallaflow` from the user's `PATH` and re-checks `yallaflow --version` on every refresh. On a mismatch with what it loaded, or an incompatible `config.yaml yallaflow.minimumVersion`, it goes read-only and shows a banner. | ## 3. Options evaluated | # | Option | Strengths | Weaknesses | Verdict | |---|---|---|---|---| | A | The brief's hypothesis: Console → Local API → Core → State | clean layering | does not say *how* the API reaches Core | refined into F′ | | B | Spawn the CLI and parse its prose output | no Core change | prose is not a contract | rejected | | C | Console reads `.yallaflow/` files directly | fast to build | duplicates Core's normalization and rules. **The prototype does this and already drifted from Core** (review finding L4: wrong gate statuses, a missing CONCLUSION rule) | **prototype only** | | D | **Static HTML export** from `--json` | no server, no security surface, shareable | not live, no actions | **ship it as a stepping stone** (Cycle 1b) | | E | IDE extension (webview) | lives in the editor | ties the Console to one IDE | later, on the same `--json` contract | | F | Service layer imported in-process (revision 1's pick) | fastest warm reads (`guide` 5 ms against 159 ms) | **version skew** with the agent's CLI; `spawnSync` git calls block the server; exposes a JS API (and on-disk shapes) under SemVer; lock re-entrancy within one process | **fallback optimization**, only if measurements demand it | | **F′** | **CLI as API:** the Console spawns `yallaflow … --json` asynchronously, with watcher-driven invalidation and per-item refresh | the same binary, version and validation as the agent; spawns are async, so the server never blocks; the public contract is JSON Schema, not JS internals; writes inherit CLI locking; parity is trivial | about 150 ms startup per spawn; initial load at 1,000 items depends on Core's read-path fixes | **recommended** | | G | Squad-Kit-style orchestrator | the full "do it for me" experience | lock-in, security surface, against governance | rejected for Core; a Cycle 4 study only, as a separate package | **Why F′ is fast enough** [Measured]: - spawns scale with *changes*, not with page views; - refreshing one item costs one `guide --json`-style call, about 160–280 ms; - the live-update target of 1 s p95 leaves room for that; - the initial load is one `snapshot --json`. | Initial load | Today | After the read-path fixes | |---|---|---| | 23 items | about `status` + `context status`, ≈0.5 s | — | | 200 items | ≈1.8 s | under 1 s, hypothesized: hashing drops 390 → 17 ms at 990 facts, and `brief`'s doctor call accounts for 97% of its in-process time | | 1,000 items | ≈6.5 s | the prerequisite fixes are needed to reach usable times | ## 4. Diagrams ### 4.1 System context ```mermaid flowchart LR Dev(["Developer / Tech lead / PM
(browser on the same machine)"]) AgentC(["Claude Code"]) & AgentX(["Codex"]) Git[("Git remote
(Shared Project)")] subgraph Machine["Developer machine"] CLI["yallaflow CLI
(the user's installed version)"] Con["YallaFlow Console
(optional package, 127.0.0.1)"] WS[(".yallaflow/ in the repo")] end Dev -- "HTTP + event stream (token, loopback)" --> Con AgentC & AgentX -- "instruction files + CLI" --> CLI Con -- "spawns: yallaflow … --json" --> CLI CLI --> WS WS -. "fs.watch (invalidation only)" .-> Con WS -- "ordinary git push/pull by the developer" --- Git ``` ### 4.2 Containers and components ```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph UI["Console UI: static, prebuilt (React + TS)"] R["Views: Home, Overview, Board, Inspector, Memory, Evidence, Agent"] QC["Query cache; invalidated by events"] BC["BroadcastChannel leader: one stream per browser"] end subgraph Srv["@yallaflow/console server (node:http, 0 runtime deps)"] Sec["Security middleware
Host allowlist · token · Origin · CSP"] API["GET /api/v1/... (read models)
POST /api/v1/actions/... (Cycle 3)"] EVT["GET /api/v1/events (fetch-stream, Authorization header)"] Cache["JSON cache per project
(snapshot + per-item entries + rev)"] Inv["Invalidation table
(path pattern → views)"] Wt["fs.watch recursive on .yallaflow/
+ 5 s stat poll fallback"] Run["CLI runner: async spawn, queue,
concurrency 2, timeout, version check"] end subgraph Core["yallaflow (existing package, the user's install)"] J["--json on read commands (NEW)
snapshot --json (NEW)"] M["Mutating commands (unchanged; lock in Core)"] Dom["Existing domain modules"] end FS[(".yallaflow/")] R --> QC --> Sec --> API & EVT BC --> EVT API --> Cache Cache -- "miss / invalidated" --> Run --> J --> Dom --> FS API -- "Cycle 3 actions" --> Run --> M --> Dom FS -. events .-> Wt --> Inv --> Cache Inv --> EVT ``` ### 4.3 Read and live update ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant A as Agent participant FS as .yallaflow/ participant W as Watcher participant C as Console cache participant R as CLI runner participant B as Browser B->>C: GET /board (ETag) C-->>B: 200 (from cached snapshot) A->>FS: yallaflow advance PF-0042 (meta.yaml, state, progress.md) FS-->>W: change events W->>W: debounce 150 ms, coalesce W->>C: invalidate(work PF-0042) via invalidation table C->>R: yallaflow work show PF-0042 --json (async spawn) R-->>C: JSON (schema v1, same version as the agent's CLI) C-->>B: event {type:"work.changed", ids:["PF-0042"], rev:118} B->>C: GET /work/PF-0042 (If-None-Match) C-->>B: 200 or 304 Note over C,B: On reconnect with a stale rev, or a git checkout (many paths change at once),
send "resync", rerun snapshot --json, and refetch everything. ``` ### 4.4 State ownership ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph Canonical["Canonical: files in the repo (ownership unchanged)"] C1["cli-owned ledgers, meta, context/index.yaml"] C2["projections"] C3["work.md narrative (shared)"] C4["config.yaml (human)"] end subgraph Derived["Derived: never canonical"] D1["Console JSON cache (memory)"] D3["UI preferences (localStorage)"] end subgraph Local["Local, never committed"] L1["~/.config/yallaflow-console/config.json
(token 0600, port, project registry)"] L2[".yallaflow/local/ (existing; lock in Cycle 1c)"] end CLI["yallaflow CLI (the only writer)"] --> C1 & C2 Agent --> C3 Human --> C4 C1 & C2 & C3 & C4 --> CLI -->|"--json"| D1 --> UI["Console UI"] ``` ### 4.5 Agent integration ```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph Today["Cycles 1–3: unchanged for agents"] AG["Claude Code / Codex"] --> IF["CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md → .yallaflow/AGENT.md"] AG --> CLI2["yallaflow"] CON["Console"] -->|"guide/handoff --json"| CLI2 H["Human"] -->|"answers in the agent session, the CLI, or (C3) the Console"| CLI2 end subgraph Later["Cycle 4 study: optional @yallaflow/agent-adapter"] AD["Adapter"] -->|"ACP (default)"| ACP["claude-agent-acp / codex-acp / gemini --acp"] AD -->|"native"| N1["claude -p stream-json + permission-prompt-tool"] AD -->|"native"| N2["codex app-server"] AD -->|"edit permission? ask"| GOV["yallaflow guide --json
(modification authorized?)"] AD --> SESS[".yallaflow/local/sessions/*.jsonl (local only)"] end ``` ### 4.6 Security and trust boundaries ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph Untrusted Web["Other sites in the browser
(CSRF, DNS rebinding)"] LAN["Other hosts"] LocalProc["Other same-user processes
(including agents)"] Content["Ticket text, docs, logs, narrative"] end MW["Boundary 1, HTTP: Host allowlist · Authorization header · Origin on POST · no CORS · CSP · GET has no side effects"] PG["Boundary 2, files: ID-addressed artifacts only, resolved by the CLI · realpath inside .yallaflow/ · no symlinks"] WG["Boundary 3, mutation: only spawned CLI commands · Core lock · actor recorded as unverified attestation"] Web -.-x MW LAN -.-x MW LocalProc -. "can read the 0600 token, like the CLI: attestation, not authentication" .-> MW Content -->|"escaped, re-redacted, sandboxed iframe"| UIR["UI rendering"] MW --> PG --> WG ``` ### 4.7 Future managed execution (concept only) ```mermaid flowchart LR Board["Console board"] -->|"start lane (human)"| Orch["@yallaflow/execution (optional)"] Orch -->|"git worktree add (adapter-owned dir)"| WT["worktree per work item"] Orch -->|"role → already-pinned skill"| AD2["agent adapter"] AD2 -->|"runs yallaflow inside the worktree"| CLI3["yallaflow"] Orch -->|"budget/turn caps; pause between steps"| AD2 Orch -.->|"never: commit, merge, push, release, approve"| X["human"] ``` ## 5. Technology evaluation | Concern | Candidates | Evidence | Recommendation | |---|---|---|---| | HTTP server | **node:http** vs Hono 4.13 vs Express | Hono: 0 deps, 1.27 MB unpacked, plus `@hono/node-server` (137 KB). The Console needs about 15 GET routes, 1 stream and about 6 POSTs. | **node:http** with a small router. It needs no dependencies, matching Core's discipline. Switch to Hono if routes pass about 40. | | Live updates | SSE (`EventSource`) vs fetch-streamed events vs WebSocket vs polling | `EventSource` cannot send an `Authorization` header. HTTP/1.1 allows 6 connections per origin. | **Fetch-streamed `text/event-stream` with the header.** A `BroadcastChannel` leader tab holds the only stream and fans out to other tabs. Events carry invalidations only. | | File watching | `fs.watch` recursive vs chokidar 6 | Measured on Linux, Node 20.16 and 22: new directories and temp+rename writes reported in about 5 ms | **fs.watch** on `.yallaflow/` plus a 5 s `stat` poll fallback; poll-only on NFS, WSL `/mnt` and container bind mounts. macOS and Windows: **unverified**. | | Core access | CLI `--json` (F′) vs in-process import (F) | Warm in-process `guide`: 5 ms; spawn: 159 ms. Heavy reads gain little either way (`status` at 200 items: 1,007 ms in-process against 1,417 ms spawned). | **F′.** Revisit F only if Cycle 1 targets are missed after the Core fixes. | | UI | **React 19 + TS + Vite, prebuilt** vs Preact 11 vs vanilla | react-dom 19.3 bundles to roughly 45–60 KB gzipped (approximate); Preact is about 5 KB gzipped. The vanilla prototype (about 500 dense lines) re-renders whole views. | React, prebuilt (dev dependencies only). Preact is acceptable if size wins (D4). | | Graphs | d3-force vs none | Lineage chains are linear (max depth 5) | No graph library. A lineage strip plus a timeline. | | Server language | JS vs TS | Core is plain JS | Plain JS with JSDoc for the server; TS only for the UI | **Budgets:** - Console tarball ≤ 1.5 MB, with 0 runtime dependencies; - initial-route UI ≤ 250 KB gzipped; - Core unchanged at 4 dependencies. **Packaging:** the Console declares `yallaflow` as a **`peerDependency`** (`>=1.2.0 <2`) for documentation only. At runtime it uses the `yallaflow` on `PATH`, the same binary the agent uses, and refuses to start if that binary is older than the required `--json` schema version. ## 6. Data changes and new artifacts "No schema change" means **no change to any existing file's schema**. These artifacts are new: | Cycle | Change | Kind | Compatibility | |---|---|---|---| | 1a | `--json` on `brief`, `status`, `guide`, `handoff`, `resume`, `context status/show/history`, `verify list`, `doctor`, `convergence status`, `qc status`, `demo status`. New `work show --json` and `snapshot --json`. All carry `{schema: "yallaflow./v1"}`. | new output contract (JSON Schema, SemVer-covered) | Text output unchanged | | 1a | Read-path fixes P1–P7 (hash memoization, no doctor in `brief`, DONE shortcut, per-request load cache, `--no-optional-locks`, lazy imports) | code | Behavior unchanged; verified by golden tests | | 1c (Core 1.2.x track, gates Cycle 3) | Lock at **`.yallaflow/local/lock`**, added to `STATE_OWNERSHIP`; `init` and `upgrade` print a `.gitignore` hint for single-user workspaces, never editing `.gitignore` silently. Unique temp names, atomic `writeYaml`, retry on `EPERM`/`EBUSY` (Windows), exclusive-`mkdir` IDs, verify's V-### allocated once. | new local file + code | Old CLIs ignore the lock, so **mixed versions writing concurrently is unsupported**. Enforce through `minimumVersion`. | | 3 | Optional `attestation` on gate responses, question answers, baseline and demo approvals, and knowledge promotion: `{recordedVia: "cli"\|"console"\|"adapter", claimedBy?: string, verified: false}`. **No default human name.** `claimedBy` is set only when a human typed it. | additive field in committed ledgers | Old readers ignore it. **Not reversible once committed**, so the owner must approve it (D6). | | 3 | Optional `artifactHash` on gate approvals (the hash of the spec/plan the human saw) | additive | Same | | 3 (decision D7) | Structured stage history: keep parsing `progress.md` in Core and expose it in `work show --json` (recommended), or add `progress.yaml stages[]` | — | Recommend parsing until a need is measured | | 4 | `.yallaflow/local/sessions/*.jsonl` | local only | Never committed | | Console | `~/.config/yallaflow-console/config.json` (0600): token, port, registered project roots | user-local | — | **One command surface (fixes review L1):** - the Console binary is `yallaflow-console`, with `start`, `add `, `remove `, `export --out ` and `open`; - Core gains **no** console subcommand; - `yallaflow console` is not added; the docs point to the separate package. ## 7. API surface (Cycle 1 draft) All endpoints sit under `/api/v1`. Payloads are the CLI's `--json` schemas (plus `rev`), so **the Console's API and the CLI's contract are the same contract.** | Method | Path | CLI source | |---|---|---| | GET | `/projects` | console config, plus `yallaflow brief --json` per project | | GET | `/projects/:p/snapshot` | `yallaflow snapshot --json` (cached) | | GET | `/projects/:p/work/:id` | `yallaflow work show --json`. Includes `evaluateAdvance({mutate:false})` blockers (which also covers gates that were never requested), guidance and the delivery summary | | GET | `/projects/:p/needs-you` | derived from the snapshot's per-item **Core blockers**, never from raw `reviews.yaml` | | GET | `/projects/:p/memory` | `yallaflow context status --json` + `context list --json` | | GET | `/projects/:p/memory/:ctx` | `yallaflow context show --json` + `context history --json` | | GET | `/projects/:p/evidence` | `verify list --json`, `convergence status --json`, `qc status --json`, `demo status --json` | | GET | `/projects/:p/work/:id/runs/:v/log?offset=&limit=` | a new `yallaflow verify log --offset --limit` (redacted, max 256 KB) | | GET (stream) | `/events` | Console-internal invalidation stream | | POST (C3) | `/projects/:p/work/:id/questions/:q/answer` | `yallaflow question answer --id Q --answer TEXT --via console [--claimed-by NAME]` | | POST (C3) | `/projects/:p/work/:id/gates/:g/approve` | `yallaflow approve --stage G --note TEXT --artifact-hash H --via console`. **Offered only when Core reports that gate as the current blocker.** | **Proposed CLI additions used above** (none exist today): every `--json` flag, `work show`, `snapshot`, `verify log`, and the `--via` / `--claimed-by` / `--artifact-hash` options. The existing commands they extend are `brief`, `status`, `guide`, `handoff`, `resume`, `context status|list|show|history`, `verify list`, `convergence status`, `qc status`, `demo status`, `question answer` and `approve` (see `src/cli.js` USAGE). **Not exposed:** - source originals; - `local/`; - any path-addressed read; - verification or shell execution; - stage advance; - checkpoints. ## 8. Cache invalidation table (fixes review M4) | Changed path | Invalidates | |---|---| | `work//**` | that item, its parent (if `meta.parent`) and its children (`decomposition.yaml`), Home and Needs-you aggregates | | `context/index.yaml` | memory, overview, Needs-care, every item's knowledge tab | | `config.yaml` | **everything** (interaction mode changes every item's guidance) | | `state/current.yaml`, `local/state/**` | Home, the Agent view | | `sources/**` | the source list, the Sources panel of linked items | | more than 50 paths within 1 s (git checkout, pull) | full resync | | repository files outside `.yallaflow/` | **not watched.** Memory freshness shows "checked at " with a **Recheck** button, plus a 60 s TTL while the Memory view is open. This addresses review H1: freshness is always Core's SHA-256 result, never an mtime guess. | ## 9. Guarantees and how they are enforced 1. **Read-only GETs.** A contract test hashes `.yallaflow/` and `.git/index` before and after every GET and every `--json` command, on all fixtures. 2. **No direct writes.** The Console source contains no `fs.write*` outside its own config file, enforced by a lint rule and a grep test. All mutations go through `spawn('yallaflow', …)`. 3. **Same validation and version.** The Console runs the user's own CLI. On a version mismatch it becomes read-only. 4. **Auditability.** Console actions add `attestation.recordedVia = "console"` and land in the same ledgers. 5. **Human gates, stated honestly.** The Console requires a human-typed note and the `artifactHash` of what was shown. **It cannot prove that a human clicked**, because any same-user process can read the token, just as any process can run the CLI today. The UI and the ledgers label console approvals "unverified attestation". **No AGENT.md rule gives console approvals extra weight.** ## 10. Rejected ideas - **SQLite read cache.** Not needed at the measured scale; a JSON cache in memory is enough. - **Console inside the `yallaflow` package.** It would add frontend assets to every install. - **Force-directed knowledge graph.** It would imply relationships that are not stored. - **A `YALLAFLOW_NO_LOCK` escape hatch.** Any agent could set it. A stale lock is handled by `yallaflow doctor` (report) plus a human-run `yallaflow doctor --clear-lock` on the same host. The lock is never stolen automatically across hosts. ## 11. Changes made after the independent review | Review finding | Change | |---|---| | C1: actor defaults misattribute agent-relayed approvals; console approvals given extra trust | `attestation` model with `verified: false`, no default name, no AGENT.md elevation (§6, §9.5) | | C2: version skew between the Console's Core and the agent's CLI | F′: the Console spawns the user's CLI, with a version check per refresh (§2, §5) | | H1: an mtime-keyed freshness cache diverges from Core; repo edits are not watched | freshness always comes from the CLI; Recheck plus TTL (§8) | | H2: `spawnSync` git in the server; `.git/index` writes | async spawns; `--no-optional-locks` (P6); `.git/index` in the contract test | | H3: an exported JS API leaks on-disk shapes into SemVer | the public contract is versioned JSON Schemas only; no JS `exports` | | H4: the `--json`-first option was not evaluated | added F′ (recommended) and D as a stepping stone | | H5: lock holes (re-entrancy, cross-host, NFS, scope, bypass, gitignore) | lock in `local/`, explicit critical sections (never held while verify's command runs), no bypass env var, no cross-host stealing, NFS unsupported | | H6: Windows rename failures | retry on `EPERM`/`EBUSY` plus Windows CI before Cycle 1c | | M1: SSE cannot send the auth header; connection limit | fetch-stream plus a `BroadcastChannel` leader | | M2: Needs-you misses gates that were never requested | Needs-you is derived from Core blockers | | M3: "no schema change" overstated | restated, with the new artifacts listed (§6) | | M4: invalidation under-specified | invalidation table (§8) | | M5: gates can be approved before they are requested | approve is offered only when Core reports that gate as the blocker, and requires `artifactHash` |
